tasks.title: operator stuck
tasks.task:
i keep getting this message from agents:
Found it — .zen-queue.flushing.json has a stuck, malformed entry from a past crashed run: "taskId": "--id" (a literal --id string instead of a real task id). That's a leftover mid-flush queue file, not the canonical database — it's the exact scratch file the operator uses to atomically apply writes, and it's what's jamming every write behind this bad literal-string entry. Clearing it out now.

fix it, so it stops getting stuck

notes.text: Fixed and deployed operator queue recovery from main. Invalid interrupted flushes are now preserved as timestamped .zen-queue.failed files and removed from the active flush path, so later writes continue; option-shaped task IDs such as --id are rejected before enqueue. Published build: builds\main\Zen-184-operator-queue-recovery\zen-operator.exe. Black-box regression verified quarantine, successful following write, and pre-queue rejection. Installed executable hash matches the published build.

tasks.title: Isolate concurrent operator requests
tasks.task: Replace the shared operator queue batch with one atomic request file per mutation, serialize application safely, discard permanently invalid requests, retain transient failures, prevent crash replays, and make operator reads truly read-only so multiple agents cannot overwrite each other.

requirements.text: each mutation is atomically published as its own uniquely named queue request file
a shared apply lock processes requests serially against the freshest project state and deletes successful files
permanently invalid requests are deleted without blocking later requests while transient failures remain retryable
stable request ids prevent an already-saved additive operation from being replayed after a crash
operator read commands do not save or overwrite project state
legacy shared queue files are safely migrated into isolated request files
parallel integration verification shows concurrent operator requests are preserved without queue leftovers

notes.text: Implemented isolated request-file queue, replay ledger, read-only operator reads, and legacy migration. Debug builds pass. Initial 48-process mixed read/write stress test preserved all 24 writes and left no queue files; two process exit states need investigation before completion.

Replaced shared batches with atomic one-request files, a serialized fresh-state drain, immediate invalid-request deletion, transient retry retention, a 2,048-id replay ledger, read-only operator reads, and legacy migration. Verification: 64 concurrent processes (32 reads/32 writes) had zero failures/timeouts and preserved all writes; invalid request exit 1 did not block the next valid request; duplicate request ID applied once; no queue leftovers. Debug and self-contained Release builds passed; commit b03ac56.
